messages.subject: Milkweed seeds
messages.text:
Hi, 

I purchased several packs of milkweed seed earlier this year and, according to directions, put them in the refrigerator for 30 days before planting. I’ve not had any luck- nothing has grown either time I’ve tried this process. 

After leaving them in the cold for the month, I planted them as I would any other seed. 

What’s going on? There are no directions after the “leave them in the fridge for a month” step. 

Please let me know what step I may be missing.

Thanks,

Tina Simons

Person who would love to have some milkweed plants, but it’s not happening with these seed.

messages.subject: Re: Milkweed seeds
messages.text:
Hi Tina,

Three messages without a reply is not acceptable, and I'm sorry. I'll make it right.

You're actually not missing a crazy amount, but there are a couple of things that make a real difference with milkweed:

1. After the cold stratification, the seeds need warmth AND moisture to germinate. The most reliable method is to plant them in small pots or seed trays, barely covered with soil (5mm max, or just pressed onto the surface), then cover the whole thing with a clear plastic bag or a transparent lid to create a greenhouse effect. Place them near a sunny window. This trapped warmth and humidity is what triggers germination, and without it, the seeds often just sit there.

2. Milkweed also needs sustained heat to sprout, ideally above 20°C for several consecutive days. Planting directly in the ground early in spring, when the soil is still cold, can stall everything even with perfect stratification.

Given that you've tried twice without success, I'd like to send you a new packet at no charge so you can give this method a real shot. Is your mailing address still the same as on your original order?

Our full planting guide is also here if you want more detail: https://lasclay.com/en/pages/planting-guide

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
